title: Brucie Benches 47 Points and Still Wins by 49, Philly Spoils Habib's Big Day, and Three Teams Stay Perfect
dek: Josh Allen went nuclear again, Kaushal's waiver wire took a scenic loop back to where it started, and the Buckaroo Football League already has a three-team penthouse and a three-team basement after two weeks.
body: Here is the most annoying sentence in the Buckaroo Football League right now: Ramon left 47.58 points on his bench and won by 49. No Banner only HULK beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 131.92 to 82.8 while Matthew Stafford (26.98) and Travis Kelce (20.6) watched from the sideline. It didn't matter, because Josh Allen threw up 40.82 against a 22.65 projection, the best individual week in the league. Brucie now has 309.8 points through two games, 40 more than anyone else, and his title odds climbed from 47% to 54%, so the rest of the league is officially playing for the other 46%.

Zoe ran into a buzzsaw and a bad break at the same time. Saquon Barkley gave Ghostu-Spider SZN 2.5 points on a 16.38 projection, which is a tough thing to absorb against the league's highest-scoring team. Zilgit's title odds slid from 13% to 1%, a brutal swing for a 1-1 team, but she was back on the wire right away, adding Devaughn Vele without dropping anyone. The rookie lost a game this week, not her nerve.

The commissioner had the most complete afternoon of anyone. Sonny's The Horse is Hea flattened Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 142.46 to 82.08, the highest score of the week, behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 38 points on a 15.22 projection. The scary part is that Sonny also benched Patrick Mahomes and his 28.98, so this could have been a 150-point day. The model finally took notice too: The Horse is Hea is 2-0 and its title odds jumped from 4% to 10%. JMoney, meanwhile, got 0.6 points from Malik Nabers, sits at 0-2 with a league-low 158 points, and owns a playoff probability of 1%, which is a number he understands better than anyone.

Alan had the week's most satisfying win, at least for Alan. Team Pillbert beat Kaushal's Habibsters 135.48 to 109.66 in a true coin flip, with Philly favored at just 51%, and Davante Adams turned a 13.14 projection into 35.5. The bad guy gets his first W and a title-odds leap from 4% to 13%, which actually puts him ahead of the 2-0 commissioner in the model's eyes. Alan also kept tinkering, adding Jalen Coker for Tony Pollard and swapping Sam LaPorta out for Isaiah Likely at tight end.

Then there's Habib, who had two of the week's six best performances and still lost. CeeDee Lamb went for 31.3 and Dak Prescott added 29.76, a Cowboys stack that delivered 61 points, and Habibsters fell by 26 anyway. The waiver activity was its own adventure: Kaushal went Jaguars D/ST to Buccaneers D/ST to 49ers D/ST and back to Buccaneers D/ST, and dropped Wan'Dale Robinson for Deebo Samuel Sr. before reversing that too. After all that speed on the transaction wire, he ended up roughly where he started, which is very on-brand for a guy whose last high-speed trip in Georgia also ended with him pulled over. The two-time champ is 0-2 with more points than 1-1 Zoe, and his playoff odds sit at 15%.

Randy won ugly, and he'll take it. The fumblers beat Mekhi's Dawgs 124.02 to 100.74 even though Caleb Williams managed just 7.72 points on a 19.42 projection, a week after carrying the team. Amon-Ra St. Brown picked up the slack with 30.7. Oddly, the win cost Randy in the projections, with his title odds falling from 28% to 21%, likely because HULK keeps hoarding the top of the distribution. Kai, a 31% underdog, made it closer than expected but drops to 0-2 with 0% title odds; he moved on from Carnell Tate for Kenyon Sadiq, and if anyone can claw back from the wire, it's him.

The standings already have a clean split: HULK, The fumblers, and The Horse is Hea at 2-0; Team Pillbert and Ghostu-Spider SZN at 1-1; Habibsters, Dawgs, and Counting or not Counting GV at 0-2. Week 3's marquee game is Habibsters against No Banner only HULK, and Kaushal's best path out of the hole runs straight through the league's best team. Zoe gets Randy in a Bears-versus-Packers showdown with way more fantasy than football on the line, Sonny tries to stay perfect against a desperate Mekhi, and Jordan gets Alan. Somebody in the basement is about to start 0-3, and at least one of those 2-0 teams is losing for the first time.

social.author: HULK Smash Society
social.text: Benched Stafford. Benched Kelce. Won by 49 anyway. We're not saying the lineup doesn't matter. We're saying it doesn't matter for US.

social.author: Habibsters Faithful
social.text: CeeDee 31.3. Dak 29.76. Loss by 26. We would like to speak to the manager of the universe.

social.author: Waiver Wire Watchdog
social.text: Habibsters D/ST journey this week: Jaguars, Bucs, 49ers, Bucs. Four stops, one round trip, zero frequent flyer miles.

social.author: The Horse Whisperer
social.text: 142.46 with Mahomes on the bench. The Horse is 2-0 and hasn't even gotten out of second gear.

social.author: BFL Insider Tony
social.text: Sources say Philly saw Davante's 35.5 and immediately started drafting his victory speech. The league is bracing.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider Web
social.text: Saquon gave us 2.5 points. TWO POINT FIVE. Shake it off, add Vele, go get Randy next week. The web is not broken.

social.author: Numbers Don't Lie Larry
social.text: HULK title odds: 54%. Rest of the league combined: 46%. Two weeks in. Somebody do something.

social.author: Fumblers Booster Club
social.text: Caleb gets 7.72 and we still win by 23. Amon-Ra, you're welcome at every family dinner from here on out.

social.author: Dawgs Pound
social.text: 0-2 but Kai is on the wire. Sadiq is in. Don't count the waiver king out in week 2, people.

bios.1: The defending champ's new outfit is 2-0 after a 142.46-point demolition of JMoney, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba leading the way. Sonny even benched Mahomes' 28.98 and still posted the week's top score. Title odds are up to 10%, and the worst-to-first sequel is off to a strong start.
bios.2: Randy is 2-0 and has won with Caleb Williams booming and busting, which says a lot about the depth. Amon-Ra St. Brown carried this week's win over the Dawgs. The title odds dipped to 21%, but a 92% playoff chance is a pretty good thing to grumble about.
bios.3: JMoney is 0-2 with a league-low 158 points after an 82.08 showing against Sonny. Malik Nabers' 0.6 points summed up the day. The playoff odds read 1%, and a matchup with Alan is up next.
bios.4: Philly bounced back from a four-point opening loss with a 135.48-point win over Habibsters, thanks to Davante Adams' 35.5. Alan has been busy on the wire, adding Jalen Coker and Isaiah Likely. At 1-1 with 13% title odds, Team Pillbert is lurking right behind the unbeatens.
bios.5: Mekhi is 0-2 after a 23-point loss to The fumblers, and the title odds have hit 0%. Kai swapped Carnell Tate for Kenyon Sadiq, and there are 12 weeks left for the waiver king to work. A game against the unbeaten commissioner is next.
bios.6: Kaushal is 0-2 despite scoring more than a 1-1 team, and this week his Cowboys stack put up 61 points in a loss. The waiver wire got a workout that ended right back where it started. The two-time champ has a 15% playoff chance and a date with the league's best team next week.
bios.7: Ramon has 309.8 points in two weeks, the league's best record, and a 54% shot at Buckaroo Bowl IV. Josh Allen has been the engine, and HULK is winning blowouts even with 47 points on the bench. The only thing standing between Brucie and a runaway season is whoever finally catches him on a bad week.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season hit its first speed bump, a 49-point loss to HULK made worse by Saquon Barkley's 2.5 points. She's 1-1 and already working the wire with Devaughn Vele. Next up is Randy, a chance to get right and win some Bears-versus-Packers bragging rights along the way.
